newsitem.title: CANADA: Go-ahead on Mercosur gas pipeline two years away.
newsitem.headline: Go-ahead on Mercosur gas pipeline two years away.

text.p: It could be two years before an international consortium makes a decision on whether to go ahead with a US$1.5 billion natural gas pipeline being studied for South America's Mercosur region, the lead company in the group said on Thursday.
"We're at the pre-feasibility stage," Dick Wilson, spokesman for Canada's Alberta Energy Co Ltd, told Reuters. "The results of that pre-feasibility are going to be presented March 25."
Other partners in the proposal, which was announced in Buenos Aires on Wednesday, include Mobil Corp, Japan's Marubeni Corp and Petrolera Argentina San Jorge.
Individual interests in the project, which would extend 1,900 miles (3,100 km) to Sao Paulo in Brazil from Salta in northwestern Argentina, had yet to be decided, Wilson said.

He said the pre-feasibility stage included initial study of the proposal and feasibility studies could take about 12 to 15 months. Results from that would yield a decision on whether to proceed with the engineering phase, he said.
Initial estimates placed the proposed line's transport capacity at 25 million cubic metres of gas per day. Construction could be completed in 2000 or 2001, the consortium said.
"It's essentially to provide a transportation service for the gas producers of northern Argentina," Wilson said, adding his firm developed the concept for the proposal.
Calgary-based AEC controls 452,000 net acres of exploration land in Argentina's Neuquen Basin and plans to drill 12 wells there this year.
Countries in South America's Mercosur customs union include Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
